profile.headline: Software engineer working on Maps JavaScript API
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer specializing in front end development. I have worked in Angular, React, Lit and raw web components and love to learn new frameworks and APIs!

I've worked extensively with mapping APIs (Leaflet, Google Maps JavaScript API and Azure Maps) to create real-time map experiences.

I have been a driving force for improving robustness, maintainability and accessibility by applying modern web development practices such as unit testing, automated build and deployment and using my own products with the assistive technology tools our clients use.

I went to school to study game development and have experience developing games using Unreal, and Unity, as well as developing my own custom game engine from scratch. My roles include developing the core engine components such as the graphics system, sound system integration, level editing and serialization, and systems that aid in creating AI such as path finding.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I develop and maintain features for the Maps JavaScript API
- Introduced web components to allow declarative use of the Maps JS API
- Implemented and updated features to improve accesability across our interactive widgets
- Updated logging tooling to improve event tracking
- Improved the API's documentation generator to ensure accuracy

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
Worked on Smartbuilding Indoor Map and location services designed for Microsoft employees and clients. Accessible as a web app via kiosks in the building, your mobile phone or desktop it could help employees navigate through any of the buildings globaly available at microsoft, find coworkers and meetings and tell you what was for lunch!
 
Personal Involvement:
- Managed the build pipeline including automated testing and code quality, and deployment
- Designed significant portions of the front end architecture (in Angular)
- Managed a migration from Javascript to Typescript
- Managed a migration to React
- Leading and advising implementations of components (architecture design) css style practices.
- Championed accessibility, implementing and guiding others to making our websites accessible.
- Helped design building navigation algorithm

positions.title: Networking Intern
positions.description: My role as an intern was to develop examples for games made using the DigiPen's proprietary Zero Engine. This involved creating a server list ui and utilizing the networking API that was part of the engine to display available networked games.

positions.title: WS+ Teacher
positions.description: WS+ stands for Workshop plus, and is very similar to the ProjectFun summer workshop Digipen hosts.

positions.title: ProjectFun Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Digipen hosts summer workshops called ProjectFun. I worked there for the summer as a teaching assistant. This involved helping students and providing support to the teacher where ever they needed it. Students are taught in two weeks sessions, from 10 to 5 for 5 days a week, and by the end we have taught them what they need to know in order to build a game using the provided editor.
The main duties were managing and supporting students, and helping out the teacher where ever they might need it, and being their eyes and ears.

projects.title: Scale
projects.description: Scale is a 3D space shooter where you work cooperatively with a party of other ships over a network. My responsibilities include developing a 3D Physics Engine, and serving as the Technical Director (working with the dev team on managing tasks and making higher level design decisions with the team).

projects.title: Guardians of Nogard
projects.description:
A top-down 2D medieval hack-n-slash game where the player must fight hordes of orcs and collect gold to buy new spells and weapons to combat the forces of evil.

The game supports up to four players using game pads, but can also be played single player with mouse and keyboard.
